chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that are great with Mankind, as they are running all the time, in that they [ ... ]
chapter_note: This chapter contains no recoverable correspondential/cosmological substrate. It is dominated by editorial-hagiographic self-presentation of Mani and a Christian-facing motif centered on the name of Christ and apostolic comparison. The text operates cosmos→contemporary religious world (Christians, oaths, names, belief in Mani) rather than cosmos→cosmos mapping, and it opens with a formulaic frame.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening (“Once again he speaks”) marks the hagiographic/dialogue frame. The mention of “Christian people” anchors the topic in the editor’s contemporary religious world rather than a closed cosmological exposition.

Enumerated ‘first’ item concerns speaking the name of Christ over actions; depends on Christian devotional practice and Christ-name piety, i.e., material entering via Mani’s Christian synthesis rather than an older cosmological system.
Continues the Christian-name theme (naming devotees/children after Christ). This is social/institutional practice, not cosmological mechanism; best explained as Christian overlay material.

Oath-taking ‘by his fortune and his surety’ for those under his authority remains within Christian-social application (cultic/communal practice around Christ), not a self-contained cosmic correspondence.

First-person Mani self-identification (“And I, Manichaios…”) and claims of grace, revelation, followers called by his name, and ‘apostolate’ are characteristic hagiographic legitimation within the compiled Kephalaia frame, not impersonal substrate teaching.

Rhetorical self-exaltation, comparison with ‘brothers the apostles who were before me,’ and an appeal to belief in Mani leading to inheritance in the ‘new aeon’ reflect community-facing proclamation/application rather than cosmological mapping; fits the later hagiographic/apostolic frame (with strong application voice).
